note: Exact pointed forms (taamim, dagesh and maqaf ignored) where the rule engine in src/pronunciation/ needs help or where a reading is open. 'applied' entries are used by the engine (kamatzKatanForms mirrors KAMATZ_KATAN_FORMS in src/pronunciation/kamatz-katan.js; a test keeps them equal). 'candidate' entries are NOT applied: they record a possible reading for a native reviewer. Nothing here has been checked by a native speaker.

kamatzKatanForms.reason: Lesson r32 teaches this as a kamatz katan example: kamatz reads o and the shva after it is silent, so the respelling is kodsho in every tradition (was kadesho).

ruleNotes.reason: Not a per-word exception: kamatzKatanStemStart now accepts conjunctive vav plus one more prefix before a listed stem (כָּל), so וּבְכָל, וּלְכָל, וּמִכָּל respell with o (uvekhol), matching the V'ahavta reading and r32 כָּל = kol. The כָּל stem itself is still unverified (kamatz-katan.js).

candidates.candidate: sh'mei (a reviewer note says the Aramaic phrase is commonly read this way; unverified)
candidates.reason: Initial shva is vocal by rule B1; whether the Aramaic reading drops it is not rule-derivable.

candidates.candidate: ne'dar (alef closing a syllable written as an apostrophe, as in ya'er)
candidates.reason: Alef with a silent shva is not a consonant sound in the engine, so it is dropped; whether the learner-facing spelling should show a glottal stop is a style decision for a reviewer.
